tasks.title: A button has no accessible name
tasks.problem: A <button> has no visible text, aria-label, aria-labelledby, title, or image alternative.
tasks.reason: Screen-reader users hear only “button” and cannot tell what the control does (WCAG 4.1.2, 1.1.1). Icon-only menus and close buttons are a common case.
tasks.fix: Add a visible text label, or an aria-label that names the action (for example “Open menu” or “Close”). Decorative SVGs inside the button should be aria-hidden="true".

tasks.title: The heading outline skips a level
tasks.problem: A heading jumps more than one level, for example from h1 to h3 or from h2 to h4. Observed pattern: h1->h3 (14 pages), h1->h5 (3 pages), h2->h6 (1 pages), h3->h5 (1 pages).
tasks.reason: Skipped levels break the document outline and make heading navigation unpredictable for assistive technology (WCAG 1.3.1).
tasks.fix: Use heading levels in order (h1, then h2, then h3). Style appearance with CSS instead of picking a level for its font size.

tasks.problem: More than one <main> element is present in the same document.
tasks.reason: The HTML specification allows only one <main> visible at a time. Multiple mains make landmark navigation ambiguous.

tasks.title: The same id is used more than once on the page
tasks.problem: One or more id values appear on multiple elements in the same document. Observed pattern: 5 unique ids duplicated; referenced=0 (25 pages), 6 unique ids duplicated; referenced=0 (11 pages), 7 unique ids duplicated; referenced=0 (6 pages), 9 unique ids duplicated; referenced=0 (2 pages).
tasks.reason: IDs must be unique. Duplicates break label-for associations, fragment links, and aria-labelledby references, so the wrong element may be named or focused.
tasks.fix: Make every id unique, typically by scoping component IDs or generating a suffix. Audit label for, aria-labelledby, and skip links after the change.

tasks.title: Multiple <nav> landmarks share no distinct accessible name
tasks.problem: The page has more than one <nav>, and at least one is missing a unique aria-label or aria-labelledby. Observed pattern: 2-navs_2-unlabelled (49 pages), 19-navs_17-unlabelled (4 pages), 17-navs_17-unlabelled (1 pages).
tasks.reason: When several navigation landmarks are unnamed or share a name, screen-reader users cannot tell the primary menu from footer or utility menus.
tasks.fix: Give every <nav> a unique accessible name, such as aria-label="Primary", aria-label="Section", and aria-label="Footer".

tasks.title: An SVG icon is visible but has no accessible name
tasks.problem: A non-hidden <svg> has no aria-label, aria-labelledby, or <title>, and is not marked decorative.
tasks.reason: Unlabelled SVGs may be announced as “image” or “graphic” with no name. Decorative icons should be hidden from assistive technology; meaningful icons need a name (WCAG 1.1.1).
tasks.fix: For decorative icons, add aria-hidden="true". For meaningful icons, add a short aria-label or a <title> and role="img".

tasks.title: A heading element is empty
tasks.problem: One or more heading tags have no accessible name (no text, image alternative, or ARIA label). Observed pattern: h4:1 (10 pages), h4:2 (5 pages), h2:1,h4:1 (5 pages), h2:1,h4:2 (2 pages).
tasks.reason: Empty headings are still announced as a heading with no name, which clutters the outline and fails WCAG 1.3.1 and 2.4.6.
tasks.fix: Put visible text in the heading, or remove the empty heading element if it is only being used as a spacer or hook.

tasks.title: A non-interactive element is used as a control
tasks.problem: A <div>, <span>, or other non-interactive tag is made clickable with role="button", an onclick handler, or tabindex="0". Observed pattern: span role=button tabindex=0×3, ul tabindex=0×1 (5 pages), div tabindex=0×1 (4 pages).
tasks.reason: These elements do not provide native keyboard activation or accessible names, so they often fail keyboard use and WCAG 2.1.1 and 4.1.2.
tasks.fix: Replace the element with a native <button> or <a href="…">. If a widget must stay custom, implement a complete ARIA pattern including keyboard support and an accessible name.

tasks.title: A link has no usable href
tasks.problem: An <a> element is missing href, has an empty href, uses href="#", or uses a javascript: URL. Observed pattern: empty-or-hash:1 (4 pages), empty-or-hash:1,missing-href:4 (1 pages).
tasks.reason: Links without a real destination are not reliably exposed as links, break open-in-new-tab, and are often placeholders for buttons (WCAG 2.4.4, 4.1.2).
tasks.fix: If the control navigates, give it a real URL. If it only triggers a script, use a <button type="button"> instead of an anchor.

tasks.title: A list contains invalid direct children
tasks.problem: A <ul> or <ol> has a direct child that is not an <li> (or a script-supporting element). Observed pattern: ul>div×4 (1 pages).
tasks.reason: Only <li>, <script>, and <template> are allowed as children of lists. Wrapping items in <div> or nesting a bare <ul> breaks list semantics.
tasks.fix: Move wrappers inside the <li>, or restructure so every direct child of the list is an <li>.
